description:
FOUND s492c (Opus, 2026-09-21) while probing task #1870's acceptance table.
PRE-EXISTING on 5ce155cb; unchanged by this batch.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):

    { package P9; use subs qw(sleep); sub g { sleep(0) } }
    print "f=", P9::g(), "\n";

    perl: dies at once, "Undefined subroutine &P9::sleep called"
    PCL:  HANGS.  Still hangs inside `eval { }`, and still hangs when P9 has
          an AUTOLOAD -- so %p-call-of-undefined-sub is never reached.

MECHANISM (read, not guessed): perl's own subs.pm does, for each name,
`*{"${callpkg}::$sym"} = \&{"${callpkg}::$sym"}` -- a self-referential glob
assignment, which in perl is merely a FORWARD DECLARATION (an undefined CV).
Under PCL `\&P9::sleep` on a name with no body evidently yields a code ref
that CALLS `P9::pl-sleep`, and assigning it back to that very slot makes the
function call itself.  `defined &P9::sleep` answers true afterwards (perl:
false), which is the same fact from the other side.

Any name works -- `hex`, `sleep`, `getpgrp` -- and the name does not have to
be a builtin's; what matters is `use subs` naming something that is never
defined.  A program that does that is broken, but a HANG is the worst way to
say so (rule 12's family: the sin is the silence).

FIX SHAPE (not attempted): `\&NAME` for a sub with no body must produce a code
ref that RESOLVES at call time and raises "Undefined subroutine &PKG::NAME
called" if it is still undefined -- never one whose target is the slot it is
about to be stored in.  `%p-call-of-undefined-sub` is the existing one
mechanism for that message.
subject: HANG (infinite loop, pre-existing): `use subs "NAME"` with NO sub of that name never returns -- perl dies "Undefined subroutine &P::NAME called"; subs.pm`s `*{"P::$sym"} = \&{"P::$sym"}` self-reference becomes a code ref that calls itself
